sections.heading: C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Renewal, privileges, registration and responsibility
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Renewal, privileges, registration and responsibility

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A13
The handbook says a person may apply online to reinstate driving privileges after suspension. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A13
The first minor-sanction paragraph assigns 30 days of suspension, or another period required by law, when DPS receives a traffic-violation or credential-restriction conviction record for a minor under 16. [A13]
Why it matters: needs_review:true; paragraph-specific source wording has an unresolved conflict with the following paragraph; see sec04-MINOR-SANCTION-CONFLICT.
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A13
The next minor-permit paragraph assigns suspension for 180 days or until the sixteenth birthday, whichever is longer, after a second traffic-violation conviction, a restricted-permit violation, or a felony or Class 1 misdemeanor while on an instruction or restricted minor permit. [A13]
Why it matters: needs_review:true; paragraph-specific source wording has an unresolved conflict with the preceding paragraph; see sec04-MINOR-SANCTION-CONFLICT.
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A13
The minor-sanction section says receiving a felony or Class 1 misdemeanor conviction produces a suspension lasting 180 days or until the sixteenth birthday, whichever is longer, or another period required by law. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A13
Reapplying after a felony or Class 1 misdemeanor suspension in the minor-sanction section requires a $50 reinstatement fee and the license fee. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A13
An unlicensed person under 18 who receives a violation is subject to the corresponding minor suspension described in the handbook. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A13
For an unlicensed minor, a second traffic offense, second restricted-minor-permit violation, felony or Class 1 misdemeanor leads to the handbook’s longer period of 180 days or the time until the sixteenth birthday. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A13
For a learner or restricted permit suspended after a first traffic conviction or restriction violation, the $50 reinstatement and application fees are waived unless a moving-offense conviction carries at least 6 points. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A13
A learner or restricted permit holder in the first-conviction suspension category may apply for a duplicate license. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A13
South Dakota residents must register vehicles and trailers they own and operate on public highways with the county treasurer for their home county. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A13
A vehicle brought from another state must be registered within 90 days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A13
Registration renewal is staggered according to the first letter of the owner’s last name. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A13
The renewal table assigns January to last names starting with A or B, February to C, D or E, and March to F, G or J. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A13
The renewal table assigns May to last names starting with H, I or O, June to K or L, and July to M or N. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A13
The renewal table assigns August to P, Q or R, September to S, and November to T, U, V, W, X, Y or Z. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A13
Selling or transferring a vehicle requires its certificate of title. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A13
A vehicle title should be stored securely outside the vehicle. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A13
The vehicle’s registration certificate must be carried in the vehicle at all times. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A13
Before driving or reregistering a vehicle, future financial-responsibility proof is required after license suspension or revocation tied to an uninsured-crash judgment, no-insurance conviction, vehicular homicide, DWI, or 2 reckless-driving convictions within 1 year. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A13
Most motorists establish future financial responsibility by asking their auto insurer to file an SR22 with the Driver Licensing Program. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R21 | anchor: A13
An SR22 must be sent directly by the insurer to the central administrative office, because exam stations cannot accept it. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R22 | anchor: A13
An owner of a vehicle that must be registered must continuously maintain a permitted form of financial responsibility. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R23 | anchor: A13
The handbook’s allowed financial-responsibility forms include an owner’s liability policy or a surety-company bond. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R24 | anchor: A13
Another financial-responsibility option is a certificate of deposit or securities worth $50,000 placed with the state treasurer. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R25 | anchor: A13
The handbook’s self-insurance-certificate option requires a minimum of 26 vehicles. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec04-R26 | anchor: A14
Written financial-responsibility evidence must stay in the covered vehicle and be shown to a law-enforcement officer on request. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R27 | anchor: A14
Acceptable insurance evidence includes a policy or identification card showing the insurer, policy number and coverage start and expiration dates. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R28 | anchor: A14
A state-treasurer certificate of deposit or a self-insurance certificate also qualifies as written financial-responsibility evidence. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R29 | anchor: A14
The handbook classifies a conviction for failing to maintain financial-responsibility proof as a Class 2 misdemeanor carrying 30 days in county jail, a $100 fine, or both. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R30 | anchor: A14
A conviction for failing to maintain financial-responsibility proof also brings a license suspension of at least 30 days and at most 1 year. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R31 | anchor: A14
After the financial-responsibility violation described by the handbook, SR22 insurance proof must be filed for 3 years measured from the eligibility date. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R32 | anchor: A14
Failure to file the required insurance proof causes suspension of vehicle registration, license plates and the driver license. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R33 | anchor: A14
The point system subjects a driver to suspension for accumulating 15 points within 12 consecutive months or 22 points within 24 consecutive months. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R34 | anchor: A14
When several offenses come from a single incident, points are assigned for the offense with the highest point value. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R35 | anchor: A14
The point system assigns no points for speeding, standing, parking, equipment, size or weight violations, including damage-control speed limits set by the transportation department. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R36 | anchor: A14
Out-of-state convictions receive points in the same way as convictions for conduct in South Dakota. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R37 | anchor: A14
A driver who requests a hearing receives one before point-system suspension. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R38 | anchor: A14
The point-system suspension periods are 60 days for the first suspension, 6 months for the second and 1 year for later suspensions. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R39 | anchor: A14
The points table assigns 10 points for DWI or DUI and also notes mandatory license revocation for intoxicated-driving convictions. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R40 | anchor: A14
Reckless driving carries 8 points, while eluding or attempting to elude and drag racing each carry 6 points in the handbook’s table. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R41 | anchor: A14
Failure to yield, improper passing and driving on the wrong side each carry 4 points in the handbook’s table. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec04-R42 | anchor: A14
A stop-sign or traffic-light violation carries 3 points, and another moving violation carries 2 points in the handbook’s table. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0014]

ranked.label: Pedagogic emphasis: Separate renewal, suspension, revocation, insurance and points rules.

corpus_stability.reason: The official dated snapshot is pinned, but revision frequency has not been measured. Unknown cadence remains blocked for release pending the section-A verification debt; this is not a claim that the handbook is volatile.
